mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'the difference between the number of X and Y' as the signed subtraction X - Y (preserving the order of X and Y), not as an absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement mentions 'difference between the number of X and Y' (or similar phrasing).
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between the number of A and B' as |A - B| (absolute value) instead of A - B.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements like 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N), preserving the direction of the comparison.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 5 more than B' as A = B - 5 (reversing the direction).

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement 'A has N items' appears, set A's current count to N at that moment, overriding any previous value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement directly gives a count for a person, e.g., 'A has 10 items'.
mathgap.example: Assuming a direct count like 'A has 10 items' is permanent and cannot be changed by later transfers.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the order given; apply each transfer immediately before evaluating any later relational statements, ensuring later statements see the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains both transfers and relational statements that refer to the same people.
mathgap.example: Processing all transfers after all relational statements, causing later comparisons to use outdated counts.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, translate them into (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of terms on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says something like 'The number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of Y and Z'.
mathgap.example: Converting such a statement into A = B + (C - D) (a direct assignment) instead of (A - B) = (C - D).

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by a numeric operation other than direct assignment or transfer (e.g., 'A has twice as many as B' or 'A has N fewer than B'), apply the appropriate arithmetic operation to compute the new count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement involves multiplication, division, or subtraction beyond simple addition/subtraction.
mathgap.example: Misapplying 'A has twice as many as B' as A = B + B instead of A = 2 * B.

mathgap.title: Temporal Snapshot for Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Treat each relational statement (differences, comparisons) as a constraint on the counts at the moment they appear, not on the final counts after later changes.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a relational statement is encountered in the sequence of statements.
mathgap.example: Using a relational constraint to set final values, ignoring that later transfers may change the counts.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer of All Items
mathgap.principle: If a transfer statement says a person gives all their items to another, set the giver’s count to zero and add that amount to the receiver.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer statement explicitly says the giver gives all of their items.
mathgap.example: Treating 'A gives all their items to B' as a transfer of a fixed amount, not zeroing A's count.

mathgap.title: Complete Statement Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify and extract every statement that mentions the target item (direct counts, differences, transfers, and difference equalities) to ensure no constraints are missed.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before processing any constraints.
mathgap.example: Missing a statement like 'The number of X that A has more than B equals ...', leading to insufficient constraints.

mathgap.title: Transfer with Unconstrained Giver
mathgap.principle: When a transfer involves a giver whose count is not otherwise constrained, treat the giver’s count as an unknown variable that can be solved later from other constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer mentions a giver whose count has not yet been fixed by any direct or relational statement.
mathgap.example: Assuming the giver's count is zero when it is actually an unknown that must be solved later.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The word 'difference' is often interpreted as a magnitude, causing loss of sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two names and compute X - Y, preserving the sign.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Transfers are sometimes treated as separate from the main sequence, causing later relational statements to use outdated counts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when encountered, before processing any subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Direct counts are mistakenly treated as immutable, ignoring that transfers can modify them later.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as setting the current count at that point, but allow later transfers to modify it.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The equality is read as A = B + (C - D) instead of (A - B) = (C - D).
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate difference equalities into (A - B) = (C - D) and keep both terms on each side.

mathgap.description: Incomplete processing of problem statements: stopping after a subset of constraints or ignoring many statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The solver may stop early, missing later constraints that affect the target variable.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Extract and process every statement that mentions the target item, ensuring no constraints are omitted.
